cases.name: labels_day_all
cases.note: Every label on AAPL 2024-01-02, extended-hours window, no source filter -- so human and model labels both come back, which is what a chart drawing both wants. Contains: a human interval and two human points; a 1d point and a 1m point; an rth=false 1h label with within_rth=false; five model proposals of which one is deleted; and five reviews. Review rules (ADR-027): a review is never drawn, it styles its target, highest id wins. #6 accepted, #7 rejected, #8 pending (no review), #9 rejected in round 1 then accepted in round 2. The review of #10 is an orphan: its target was deleted, so there is nothing to style and it draws nothing. #16 was deleted and is absent.

cases.name: labels_day_human
cases.note: source=human: ground truth only -- the human labels and every review.

cases.name: labels_day_model
cases.note: source=model: the live proposals. The deleted one is not here.

cases.name: labels_morning_window
cases.note: A 5m chart showing 09:30-12:00. The 1d trend_day label is stamped 16:00 yet is returned, because the filter tests coverage (cover_from_ms, cover_to_ms], not the stamp. Draw a label on every loaded bar whose own bucket intersects its coverage. On an RTH view, hide labels with within_rth=false entirely rather than clipping them.

cases.name: label_post_response
cases.note: POST /labels returns 201 and the stored label, id and derived fields assigned.

cases.name: label_patch_response
cases.note: PATCH replaces payload whole; coverage and created_at_ms never change.

cases.name: label_errors
cases.note: Error bodies are FastAPI's {"detail": str}. 422 when the store refuses a label or a patch, 404 for an unknown or deleted id. A stamp off the bar grid is refused, never snapped -- it means the timestamp did not come from a loaded bar.
